title: Insert after a node
summary: Four pointers change. The two on the new node go first, so nothing is lost.

checkpoints.text: Before: 10 and 30 point at each other. Next, 20 goes between them, right after the node `head` points at.
1 of 4: the new node points forward at 30. Its own arrows are set first because nobody depends on them yet.
2 of 4: the new node points back at 10. The list itself has not changed yet: 10 and 30 still point at each other.
3 of 4: 30 now points back at 20. `prevNode->next` still means 30 here, because 10's `next` has not changed yet.
4 of 4: 10 points forward at 20, and 20 is fully linked. If this line ran before step 3, `prevNode->next` would already be 20, and step 3 would point 20 back at itself.
10 20 30. Inserting after a known node is O(1) in a doubly linked list: no walking, just four pointers.
